title: confed admin result
description: The `result` of every `confed admin … --json`. `action` names the subcommand (`group.create`, `perms.grant`…); the fields beside it depend on it. A write under `--dry-run` carries `dry_run: true` and `planned`, and changed nothing; a write declined at the confirmation prompt carries `cancelled: true`.

dry_run.description: Present on writes. True: nothing was sent that changes the server.

planned.description: With `dry_run`: what the command would do, one sentence per change.

cancelled.description: The confirmation was declined; nothing changed.

user.description: `user.create`: the user made. `user.groups`: the user asked about, as given.

members.description: `group.members`: who is in the group. `group.add`, `group.remove`: who is in it after the change, read back from the server.

members_from.description: `group.create`, `group.add` with `--members-from`: the group whose members were copied.

already_members.description: `group.add`: the users that were in the group already. Nothing was sent for them.

not_members.description: `group.remove`: the users that were not in the group. Nothing was sent for them.

unknown_users.description: `group.add`, `group.remove`: the users the server knows nobody by. Each is also in the envelope's `errors`, with `kind: unknown_user`; the others were still changed.

users.description: `group.add`, `group.remove`, and `group.create --members-from`: the users changed — under `--dry-run` with `--members-from`, those that would be. Those that failed are in the envelope's `errors`, and make the exit 8.

mode.description: How the site grants space access: permissions one by one (Data Center, and Cloud before roles), roles, or both during the transition.

id.description: Cloud's permission id; null on Data Center.

subjects.description: `perms.list --compact`, in place of `permissions` and `assignments`: one entry per subject, with everything it holds.

subject.description: The subject as a command takes it: `group:NAME`, `user:NAME` (username on Data Center, account id on Cloud) or `anonymous`. `other:ID` for what Cloud lists and no command can name.

role_id.description: On a site that assigns roles: the subject's.

subject.description: `perms.grant`, `perms.revoke`, and `perms.list` and `perms.copy` with `--subject`: `group:NAME`, `user:NAME` or `anonymous`, as given.

as.description: `perms.copy --as`: who the permissions were granted to instead.

to.description: `perms.copy`: the space that was granted in.

copied.description: `perms.copy`: one entry per subject, in the order the source lists them.

skipped.description: `perms.copy`: subjects of the source that nothing can be granted to, each with why.

held.description: `perms.grant`, `perms.revoke` with `--op`: every operation the subject holds in the space after the change, read back from the server.

from.description: Who holds the permissions in the source, as a command takes it.

subject.description: Who they were granted to: the same subject, or the one `--as` (or `--map`) names.

ok.description: False when granting to this subject failed; why is in the envelope's `errors`.

granted.description: The operations granted now — under `--dry-run`, those that would be.

already_granted.description: The operations the subject held in the destination already. Nothing was sent for them.

held.description: Every operation the subject holds in the destination after the copy, read back from the server. Absent under `--dry-run`.

role_id.description: On a site that assigns roles: the role the subject has in the source.

role_assigned.description: Whether that role was assigned now; false when the subject had it already, or it failed.

id.description: Cloud's group id; null on Data Center, which knows a group by name.
The userkey or account id; the group's name on Data Center, its id on Cloud.

name.description: Who it is, when the server could say.

username.description: A Data Center user's username, which is how `user:NAME` names them.
